text: Wheatstone's cryptograph looks like a clock: move the long hand forward to each plain letter and read the letter under the short hand on a mixed inner ring. The hands drift, so repeated letters come out differently.

Inside each known word the hand's steps are known, so the known letters say where each carved letter sits on the inner ring, up to one turn per word. A ring in any order, or mixed from any dictionary word; K4 and twenty scrambled copies.
Nothing fits, not even a ring in any order: in every set-up some carved letter would have to stand at two places of the inner ring, or two letters at one. F10.2 closed.
